failures.title: Lexus V35A-FTS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Main bearing failure (oil starvation) - all V35A-FTS units, 2017-mid-2024
items.onset: As low as 10,500 miles; commonly 25,000-60,000 miles
items.whatHappens: The V35A-FTS has been subject to multiple major recalls affecting nearly 270,000 vehicles worldwide since 2024. Toyota attributes the failures to machining debris (swarf) left inside the engine during production, which obstructs oil passages and starves critical components. In practice, the failure manifests as spun main bearings - teardowns show main bearings "spun inside their saddles, causing heat damage, scoring, and metal transfer onto the crankshaft". Owners report engine knocking, rough running, failure to start, or sudden loss of motive power at speed. A design change was made to the V35A-FTS in July 2024. Read our full engine failure guide .
items.repairVsReplace: Main bearing failure typically writes off the engine - the crankshaft and block are frequently damaged beyond economical repair. Complete engine replacement is the standard remedy. Toyota has been replacing affected engines under recall, but only for vehicles that meet specific criteria.

items.title: Timing chain and phaser wear - all V35A-FTS units
items.whatHappens: The V35A-FTS uses a chain-driven timing system with VVT-iE (intake) and VVT-i (exhaust) phasers. Specialist reports indicate that "phasers will obviously cause problems, the timing chain won't live long". Direct-injection engines like the V35A-FTS are also demanding on fuel quality - poor-quality fuel can accelerate carbon buildup and phaser wear. Read our full timing chain failure guide .
items.repairVsReplace: Phaser and chain replacement is a significant job requiring specialist tools and expertise. If caught early before chain failure causes valve/piston contact, repair is viable. If timing fails completely, the engine is likely beyond repair.

items.title: Turbocharger wastegate and oil consumption issues
items.whatHappens: A secondary defect matrix is emerging on the V35A-FTS, with "electronic turbocharger wastegate failures and localized oil consumption" presenting a significant out-of-warranty threat. The twin-turbo system adds complexity and potential failure points beyond the main bearing issue.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo repairs (£1,500-£3,000 per turbo) are typically viable if caught early. However, if turbo failure contaminates the engine with metal debris, full engine replacement may be required.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the V35A-FTS
variants.intro: The V35A-FTS is a single engine code with multiple output tunes across different applications. Unlike European engines with dozens of sub-codes, the V35A-FTS uses a consistent internal architecture with ECU calibration differences between models. Where to find your engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped plate on the front or side of the V6 - On your V5C registration document - engine number section - Via Lexus VIN lookup - your dealer can confirm from the chassis number Power output by model (all V35A-FTS): | Model | Power | Torque | Notes | |-------|-------|--------|-------| | Lexus LS500 | 416 hp | 442 lb-ft (600 Nm) | Flagship saloon tune | | Lexus LX600 | 409 hp | 479 lb-ft (650 Nm) | SUV tune, lower peak rpm | | Lexus GX550 | 354 PS (349 hp) | 479 lb-ft (650 Nm) | Detuned for off-road durability | Interchange note: Not all V35A-FTS units are directly interchangeable - oil pan, sump, and engine mount configurations differ between longitudinal (LS, LX, GX) applications. The LS500 uses a different oil pan and mounting arrangement than the LX600/GX550. Always confirm the exact donor vehicle match before purchasing a replacement unit . What about Toyota-badged versions? The same engine code in the Land Cruiser 300, Tundra, and Sequoia uses the same block and rotating assembly but different ECU calibration, ancillaries, and sometimes different turbocharger specifications. A Lexus V35A-FTS may not be a straight swap into a Toyota application without additional modifications.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement V35A-FTS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used V35A-FTS **only makes sense with full provenance** - you need documented evidence that the donor vehicle was **not subject to the main bearing recall**, or that the recall work has been completed. Given the catastrophic failure mode, a used engine without history is a high-risk gamble. If the donor vehicle is post-July 2024 production, the risk is significantly lower. Used units from LS500s (lower-stress saloon application) may be preferable to those from LX600s (high-stress SUV application) . Learn more about used engines .

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned V35A-FTS is the **safest bet for out-of-warranty replacement** - the rebuild should address the main bearing issue (upgraded bearings, thorough cleaning of all oil galleries to remove any debris), replace timing chain and phasers, and rebuild the turbos. Given the known failure mode, a recon unit with **upgraded main bearings and documented oil gallery cleaning** is worth the premium over a used engine. Learn more about reconditioned engines .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for high-value hosts (LX600, LC300) where the vehicle value exceeds £40,000-£80,000. The rebuild should include: **crankshaft inspection/regrind, new main and rod bearings (upgraded specification), new timing chain and phasers, turbocharger rebuilds, and full oil system flush**. Given the labour intensity (cab-off procedure on some models), a rebuilt engine from a specialist with V35A-FTS experience is essential. Learn more about rebuilt engines .

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** Replacing a V35A-FTS through our network connects you with Lexus-specialist workshops who understand the specific requirements of this engine, including the recall implications and proper oil gallery cleaning procedures. Learn more about supply and fit . --- **VEHICLE VALUE NOTE - mandatory read before committing:** The V35A-FTS sits in **high-value hosts** - LS500 (£15,000-£45,000 used), LX600 (£40,000-£80,000+), and GX550 (£50,000-£80,000+) . Replacement costs of £6,500-£13,000 represent **15-30% of vehicle value** on most examples, making replacement financially viable for all but the oldest, highest-mileage examples. **However:** If your vehicle is **covered by the active Toyota/Lexus recall**, you may be entitled to a **free replacement engine** - do not pay for a replacement before confirming recall status with your Lexus dealer. If your vehicle is **not covered** and the vehicle value is approaching the replacement cost (sub-£15,000 LS500s), evaluate scrap/part-exchange value carefully before committing to a £6,500+ replacement.

items.question: How much does a Lexus V35A-FTS engine replacement cost in the UK?
items.answer: A replacement V35A-FTS typically costs between £6,500 and £13,000 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit (supply only), plus £1,500-£2,400 for fitting. Used units are cheaper at £3,500-£6,000 but carry higher risk due to the known main bearing failure issue. Reconditioned: £6,500-£9,500 supply only. Rebuilt: £8,500-£13,000 supply only. Fitting labour: 14-20 hours at £75-£120/hr. Always check if your vehicle is covered by the manufacturer recall before paying for a replacement - many owners qualify for a free engine.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the V35A-FTS engine?
items.answer: The most serious and widespread failure is main bearing failure caused by machining debris left inside the engine during production. This can happen at as little as 10,500 miles and leads to oil starvation, spun bearings, and catastrophic engine damage. Toyota issued a global recall affecting nearly 270,000 vehicles. The recall covers many 2018-2024 LS500, LX600, and Toyota Land Cruiser 300/Tundra models. Post-July 2024 production units received a design change and are not affected. Symptoms include knocking, rough running, and sudden loss of power.

items.question: Which Lexus models use the V35A-FTS engine?
items.answer: The V35A-FTS is fitted to three Lexus models: Lexus LS (XF50, 2017-present) - LS500, 416 hp; Lexus LX (J310, 2021-present) - LX600, 409 hp; and Lexus GX (J250, 2023-present) - GX550, 349 hp (detuned). The engine is also used in Toyota-badged SUVs and trucks, but those applications have different engine mounts and calibrations.

items.question: Is the V35A-FTS covered by a manufacturer recall?
items.answer: Yes - in 2024, Toyota issued a global recall affecting nearly 270,000 vehicles with the V35A-FTS, including Lexus LS, LX, and GX models. The recall addresses the main bearing debris issue and provides a free engine replacement for affected vehicles. Coverage depends on model year, production dates, and region. UK vehicles (including grey imports) may be covered - contact your Lexus dealer with your VIN. Do not pay for a replacement engine until you confirm recall status - you could be eligible for a no-cost replacement.

items.question: Should I buy a used V35A-FTS engine or go for a reconditioned unit?
items.answer: A reconditioned V35A-FTS is strongly preferred over a used unit because the recon process addresses the known main bearing issue (upgraded bearings, thorough oil gallery cleaning, new timing components). Used engines are a gamble - they may have debris still present and could fail soon after installation. Used: only consider with full provenance and confirmation that the donor was post-July 2024 or had the recall work completed. Reconditioned: the safest option with a 12-24 month warranty. Rebuilt: best for high-value hosts (LX600, LC300) where the vehicle is worth keeping long-term.

items.question: How do I identify if my engine is the V35A-FTS?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the engine block (usually on the front or side of the V6) and appears on your V5C registration document. You can also confirm via a Lexus VIN lookup - your dealer can identify the exact engine from the chassis number. Check the engine bay for a metal plate with 'V35A-FTS'. Look at the V5C under 'Engine number' - the code is the first part. If you are unsure, enter your registration above and we will confirm your fitment.
